The mass of the pendulum clock, m = 2.45 kg
Effective length, l = 100 cm = 1 m
Acceleration due to gravity, g = 9.8 ms⁻²
Now, T = 2π√(m/k) = 2π√(L/g)
⇒ √(m/k) = √(L/g)
⇒ m/k = L/g
⇒ k = mg/L = (2.45 × 9.8)/1 = 24.01 Nm⁻¹
The spring constant of the clock is 24.01 Nm⁻¹ (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"In the light of stem how long will the clock run slowly in one day in space? Analyze mathematically.","marks":4,"answer":"Here,
The radius of earth, R = 6000 km
Height in space, h = 900 km
We know, g = GM/R² [at ground]
g' = GM/(R + h)² [at h height]
Dividing, we get, g'/g = R²/(R + h)²
⇒ g' = [R²/(R + h)²] × g
= [(6000 × 10³)/(6000 × 10³ + 900 × 10³)]² × 9.8
= [6000/6900]² × 9.8
= 7.41 ms⁻²
Now, time period at ground,
T₁ = 2π√(L/g) = 2 × (22/7) × √(1/9.8) = 2.007 s
Time period at height h,
T₂ = 2π√(L/g') = 2 × (22/7) × √(1/7.41) = 2.309 s
Time difference per oscillation = T₂ - T₁ = 2.309 - 2.007 = 0.302 s
Number of oscillations in one day at ground = (24 × 60 × 60)/2.007 = 43068 oscillations
Total time lost in one day = 43068 × 0.302 = 13006.5 s = 216.8 minutes = 3.61 hours (Ans.)

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is called potential energy?","marks":1,"answer":"The energy that develops in a body due to its position or change in position is known as potential energy.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why the sound of thundering is heard after a moment of lightning?","marks":2,"answer":"The sound of thunder is heard after we see lightning because light and sound travel at different speeds. Light travels extremely fast (about 3×10⁸ ms⁻¹) so we see the lightning almost instantly. However, sound travels much slower (about 340 ms⁻¹) so it takes a bit longer to reach us. That's why we see the flash of lightning first and hear the thunder after a short delay.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"From above stem calculate the frequency of sound wave.","marks":3,"answer":"Here,

We know that, V_T/V_o = √(T_T/T_o)
⇒ V_T = V_o√(T_T/T_o)

= 347.66 ms⁻¹

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Will the person can hear echo? Give your opinion with mathematical analysis.","marks":4,"answer":"Here,
Initial distance from reflector, d₀ = 16 m
Velocity of person, v_p = 20 ms⁻¹
Velocity of sound, v = 347.66 ms⁻¹
When the person produces sound and starts running away, the sound travels to the reflector and back. During this time, the person also moves away.
Time for sound to reach reflector = d₀/v = 16/347.66 = 0.046 s
Distance person moves in this time = v_p × 0.046 = 20 × 0.046 = 0.92 m
New position of person from reflector = 16 + 0.92 = 16.92 m
Time for sound to return from reflector to person = 16.92/347.66 = 0.049 s
Total time = 0.046 + 0.049 = 0.095 s < 0.1 s
Since the total time is less than 0.1 s (the persistence of hearing), the person will not be able to distinguish the echo from the original sound. Therefore, the person cannot hear the echo. (Ans.)
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

So, if the depth of the well is AC = h then, \[ h = d_1 + d_2 = (19.8 + 22.5)m = 42.3 \, \text{m} \]

The more the temperature increases, the more the velocity of sound in the air increases. Velocity of sound is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature. So, if velocity of sound is v and temperature in kelvin scale is T, then v ∝ √T. So, if absolute temperature becomes 4 times, then velocity of sound in air will be doubled. For this reason, the velocity of sound is more in summer than that in winter.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If the difference of frequency of these two waves is 250 Hz find the frequency of both waves from scene-1.","marks":3,"answer":"Let, AB = CD = L
The first wave completes 3 full oscillations
∴ Wavelength, λ₁ = L/3
The second wave completes 2.5 full oscillations
∴ Wavelength, λ₂ = L/2.5 = 2L/5
Here, Velocity of the first wave, v₁ = 400 ms⁻¹
Velocity of the second wave, v₂ = 350 ms⁻¹
Now, f₁ = v₁/λ₁ = 400/(L/3) = 1200/L
f₂ = v₂/λ₂ = 350/(2L/5) = 875/L
Given, f₁ - f₂ = 250
⇒ 1200/L - 875/L = 250
⇒ 325/L = 250
⇒ L = 325/250 = 1.3 m
Therefore, f₁ = 1200/1.3 = 923.08 Hz
f₂ = 875/1.3 = 673.08 Hz (Ans.)
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"From scene-2, draw a wavelength vs frequency graph and explain their relation.","marks":4,"answer":"From scene-2, for a particular wave:
When wavelength (λ) becomes half, frequency (f) becomes double.
This shows that v = fλ = constant
The relationship between wavelength and frequency is inversely proportional: f ∝ 1/λ or λ ∝ 1/f
Graph: The wavelength vs frequency graph will be a rectangular hyperbola. As wavelength increases, frequency decreases, and vice versa. The product of wavelength and frequency remains constant (equal to velocity).
[A curve starting high on the left (high λ, low f) and decreasing smoothly to the right (low λ, high f), approaching but never touching the axes]
This inverse relationship confirms that for a wave traveling at constant velocity, wavelength and frequency are inversely proportional to each other. (Ans.)

Hence, we do not hear every sound occurs in the environment.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Determine the wavelength of the sound called by the teacher.","marks":3,"answer":"Here, Velocity of the sound in the air, \(v = 350 \, \text{ms}^{-1}\) Frequency, f = 700 Hz
Wavelength, \(\lambda = ?\)
We know, \[v = f\lambda\] \[\Rightarrow \lambda = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{350}{700} = 0.5 \, \text{m} \, (\text{Ans})\]","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze mathematically who and how long after can hear the echo of sound of teacher's calling.","marks":4,"answer":"Here, the teacher is standing at d = (50 + 50) = 100 m away from the wall. The student is standing at 50 m away from the wall. . . . The teacher can hear the echo after, \[ t = \frac{2d}{v} = \frac{2 \times 100}{350} = 0.57 \, s \]
The student can hear the echo after, \[ t = \frac{100 + 50}{350} = 0.43 \, s \]
So, the teacher will hear the sound (0.57 - 0.43) = 0.14 s after the student heard.

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"If Rafya runs towards the reflector at the same velocity, will she hear the echo? Analyze mathematically.","marks":4,"answer":"Here,
Velocity of sound, v = 347.66 ms⁻¹
Velocity of Rafya, v_R = 10 ms⁻¹
Time to hear echo, t = 0.5 s
When running away from reflector:
Let initial distance from reflector = d₀
Total distance traveled by sound = 2d₀
Distance traveled by Rafya = v_R × t = 10 × 0.5 = 5 m
Since sound goes to reflector and comes back while Rafya moves away:
Time for sound to reach reflector = t₁
Time for sound to return = t₂
t₁ + t₂ = 0.5 s
Distance to reflector: d₀ = v × t₁
Sound returns to Rafya at position: d₀ + v_R × 0.5
Return distance: d₀ + v_R × 0.5 = v × t₂
From d₀ = v × t₁: t₁ = d₀/v
From d₀ + 5 = v × t₂: t₂ = (d₀ + 5)/v
t₁ + t₂ = 0.5
d₀/347.66 + (d₀ + 5)/347.66 = 0.5
(2d₀ + 5)/347.66 = 0.5
2d₀ + 5 = 173.83
d₀ = 84.42 m
When running towards reflector:
Sound reaches reflector in time t₁ = 84.42/347.66 = 0.243 s
In this time, Rafya moves: 10 × 0.243 = 2.43 m closer
New distance: 84.42 - 2.43 = 81.99 m
Time for sound to return: t₂ = 81.99/347.66 = 0.236 s
Total time = 0.243 + 0.236 = 0.479 s ≈ 0.48 s
Since 0.48 s > 0.1 s, Rafya will be able to hear the echo when running towards the reflector. (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Water waves are an example of transverse waves. In the case of transverse waves, the particles are moving up and down. The direction of movement is always perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. This transverse motion of the waves on the surface of the water can be visualized by thinking of a boat moving up and down in the same place as the water waves pass by.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Determine the wavelength in medium P.","marks":3,"answer":"Here,

Velocity of sound Q, \( V_q = 400 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)

We get, \[ V_q - V_p = f(\lambda_p - \lambda_p) \] \[\Rightarrow 400 - 350 = f \times 0.4\] \[\Rightarrow f = \frac{50}{0.4} \, \text{Hz} = 125 \, \text{Hz}\]
Now, Wavelength of medium P, \(\lambda_p = \frac{V_q}{f} = \frac{350}{125} = 2.8 \, \text{m} \, (\text{Ans.})\)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"What will be the difference of distance covered by the sound for 40 vibration in P and Q medium? Similarly, \[\lambda_p = \frac{V_q}{f} = \frac{400}{125} = 3.2 \, \text{m}\]
Distance travelled for 40 vibrations in medium P, \[D_p = 40 \times \lambda_p = 40 \times 2.8 = 112 \, \text{m}\]
And, distance travelled for 40 vibrations in medium Q, \[D_q = 40 \times \lambda_q = 40 \times 3.2 = 128 \, \text{m}\]
Difference between the travelled distance \[= D_q - D_p = (128 - 112) = 16 \, \text{m} \, (\text{Ans.})\]
